title: Closed-site operations under weakly etale localization
statement:
For the cartesian square obtained by a weakly etale $W\to X$ and a closed
immersion $Z\to X$, restriction to $W$ commutes with the underived closed
direct image, and the two composites of inverse images agree. These
identifications respect the unit and counit of the closed adjunction.

proof.text: Set alpha to asIso of localizationRestrictionBaseChangeMap for the flipped pullback square. The source-library theorem isIso_localizationRestrictionBaseChangeMap_of_isPullback proves invertibility. Its definition is sheafPushforwardContinuousNatTrans of pullbackMapComparison, so its component on G and T is definitionally the specified restriction map.

Let adj and adjprime be the closed pullback/direct-image adjunctions and loc and locprime the weakly etale restriction/direct-image adjunctions. Define beta inverse to be the left-adjoint isomorphism conjugate to squareLowerStarIso under adj.comp locprime and loc.comp adjprime. Apply the injective mates equivalence for locprime and loc. Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv, the inverse law of conjugateEquiv, and the source-library mateEquiv_localizationRestrictionBaseChangeMap identify the mate of beta inverse with alpha hom.

Apply Mathlib unit_mateEquiv to beta inverse and the preceding mate equality; postcompose with the local closed direct image of beta hom. Functoriality and beta inverse followed by beta hom equal identity give the displayed unit identity. Apply mateEquiv_counit to the same square; precompose with the local closed inverse image of alpha inverse. Functoriality and alpha inverse followed by alpha hom equal identity give the displayed counit identity.

blueprint_update.statement:
Consider a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
W' & \xrightarrow{\;w'\;} & Z\\
{\scriptstyle g'}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle g}\\
W & \xrightarrow{\;w\;} & X
\end{array}
$$
with $w$ (hence $w'$) weakly etale and $g$ an arbitrary morphism, for
instance a closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow X$. For pro-etale sheaves, the
inverse images along $w$ and $w'$ are restrictions to the slices over $W$ and
$W'$. The base change map
$$
 w^*g_*\longrightarrow g'_*w'^*
$$
is an isomorphism, and it corresponds, under the adjunctions $w^*\dashv w_*$
and $w'^*\dashv w'_*$, to the identification $g_*w'_*\cong w_*g'_*$ of direct
images along the two composites of the square. The two composites of inverse
images agree, $w'^*g^*\cong g'^*w^*$, both being identified with the inverse
image along the diagonal of the square. In particular restriction to $W$
commutes with the underived direct image along a closed immersion,
compatibly with the units and counits of these adjunctions.

proof.text:
By the slice identification in
[lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], restriction along a weakly
etale map is evaluation on objects over it. For an object $T\to W$ of the
slice, both $(w^*g_*G)(T)$ and $(g'_*w'^*G)(T)$ are the value of $G$ on
$T\times_XZ=T\times_WW'$, the two descriptions of this fibre product being
identified by the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Thus both
functors are precomposition with two functors of sites that are isomorphic
via the canonical comparison of fibre products, and the base change map is
induced by this isomorphism; hence it is an isomorphism. Its mate under the
restriction adjunctions is computed sectionwise: the units restrict sections
to the slices and the counits evaluate them, and unwinding these formulas
gives exactly the isomorphism of direct images along the two composites
$g\circ w'$ and $w\circ g'$ of the square. Finally, inverse images are left
adjoint to direct images, and direct images compose strictly up to canonical
isomorphism; by uniqueness of adjoints $(g\circ w')^*\cong w'^*g^*$ and
$(w\circ g')^*\cong g'^*w^*$, and $g\circ w'=w\circ g'$ gives the
agreement of the two composites of inverse images.
